order: Grant the agents that carry out work the git permissions they need to complete orders that call for committing and pushing, since a subagent cannot accept authorization relayed only through a work order's prose. The installer must merge exactly three git command patterns — add, commit, push — into the allow list in the project's settings file, and the merge must be idempotent: re-running the installer must never duplicate an entry or clobber anything already present in the file. The uninstaller must remove exactly those three grants and nothing else the user may have added since; it must never touch an unrelated permission entry. The existing guard-hook restriction that bars the Director itself from running shell commands must stay unchanged, so the new grants extend only to the agents doing the work, never to the Director. Document the change only in the README's install and permissions notes.
claims: The installer now merges exactly three git command permissions into the allow list, verified idempotent across repeated runs with no duplicate entries. The uninstaller removes exactly those three grants and nothing else. The Director remains barred from shell commands by the existing guard hook, confirmed unchanged. The diff was inspected directly: 47 insertions across 2 files, 42 of them in install.js and 8 in the README documenting the new grants.
